subject: chemistry_2
question_text: What is aqua regia? Write its equation with gold and platinum.

verification.note: Unit 9 (VIIA Group Elements) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.86-89, the sub-box "VIIA GROUP ELEMENTS" of printed chapter 7, which prints the question and a model answer. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK TYPO (book p.86, VSAQ 6): the question and answer print "Aquaregia" as one word; it is written "aqua regia" here. BOOK NOTATION CORRECTED: the platinum complex is printed "3PtCl₆⁻²", with the charge before the number. The charge is written after the subscript, so PtCl₆²⁻ is written here. BOOK GAP: the printed answer gives the ratio as "3 : 1" without saying by volume, and never says why the mixture dissolves a metal that neither acid dissolves alone; both are written here. Both printed equations were checked for atoms AND charge and balance as printed (gold: 4 H, 1 N, 3 O, 4 Cl and charge −1 on each side; platinum: 3 Pt, 16 H, 4 N, 12 O, 18 Cl and charge −6 on each side).

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What aqua regia is
lines: Aqua regia is a freshly made mixture of
concentrated HCl and concentrated HNO₃ in
It dissolves noble metals such as gold and
platinum, which neither acid dissolves on
steps.why: The nitric acid oxidises the metal to its ion, and the chloride ion from the hydrochloric acid then binds that ion as a stable complex, AuCl₄⁻ or PtCl₆²⁻. Binding the metal ion as a complex keeps the concentration of free Au³⁺ or Pt⁴⁺ very low, and that is what lets the nitric acid go on oxidising the metal. It is why the mixture works when neither acid works alone.
common_mistakes: Writing the ratio as 1 : 3. Aqua regia is three parts concentrated HCl to one part concentrated HNO₃.
Writing that it is a mixture of HCl and H₂SO₄. The oxidising acid in aqua regia is HNO₃.
steps.memory_tip: Three parts hydrochloric to one part nitric: the larger number goes with the longer name, HCl three.
steps.margin_note: Both acids, the 3 : 1 ratio and the word concentrated are needed for this mark.

steps.label: The two equations
lines: Gold goes to +3 and platinum to +4.
steps.why: Both equations balance in atoms and in charge, and the charge check is the one students skip: the gold line carries −1 on each side and the platinum line −6 on each side. The nitrate is reduced to NO in both, which is the sign that HNO₃ is doing the oxidising.
common_mistakes: Writing the complex as PtCl₆⁻². The charge is written after the subscript: PtCl₆²⁻.
Balancing the atoms but not the charge. Both sides of each equation must carry the same total charge.
steps.memory_tip: Gold takes four chlorides, platinum takes six. Both give NO, never NO₂.
steps.margin_note: Both equations are asked for in this mark. Write the gold one first, it is the shorter, then the platinum one.

insider_note: The definition mark is the one worth protecting: name both acids, say concentrated, and give the ratio 3 : 1 by volume. The equations are long and are marked generously.
